old: a Baidu account. The help-site FAQ says the verification SMS reaches Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan and 207 countries and regions, and that a number is entered as a plus sign and the country code followed by the number, so a non-mainland number can receive it. One third-party review states the account must finish a real-name step binding a phone number and an ID card before a GPU environment can start; no first-party page read states an ID document, so the ID step is reported and not documented.
new: a Baidu account. The registration form asks for a username, a phone number chosen from a country selector that lists mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan, the United States and others, a password and a captcha, and asks for no identity document. The help-site FAQ says the verification SMS reaches Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan and countries and regions outside the mainland, and that a number is entered as a plus sign and the country code followed by the number, so a non-mainland number can receive it. Whether starting a GPU notebook then requires an ID-document real-name step is unverified: behind a sign-up; the real-name page answers 'This operation requires login', no first-party page read states an ID document, AI Studio's model-creation page requires 完善身份信息 (completing identity information), and a third-party review reports a real-name step binding a phone number and an ID card before a GPU environment can start, so the kind rests on that report.
